The source was intentionally late, so these rows would be rejected as official results. The run is a control that proves the implementation's boundary invariant is false. An on-time worker preempted before its next start can reach the same path after the deadline.

C, Go, Erlang and the smaller Rust attach/detach loops cannot pass the kernellet's complete external battery. That battery includes BOOT, table bounds, finalization, fencing, authority evidence, custody and multi-context behavior that those comparators do not implement. A shim that supplies those mechanisms would test the shim, not the transition loop.
Use two different gates and name them honestly:
The production kernellet subject must pass the full current census/external battery unchanged at the exact measured commit.
Every measured row must pass one new shared

limited to the semantics actually priced: possession dispatch, generation/transition evolution, copy-in/copy-out, refusal without losing the original, and the common digest. Include a skip-copy-out mutant that this suite catches.
The marginal-subtraction prose also overstates what arithmetic guarantees. K/2K subtraction is intended to cancel costs fixed per process at constant

; it does not by itself prove that first-touch, JIT, runtime services or non-proportional GC canceled. Keep F-KC-3's K/2K/4K linearity check and rewrite the fixed-cost list as hypotheses validated by that check. If a row is nonlinear, report the raw points and withhold the marginal.
